insight.title: Why You Fill Every Empty Space You Have
insight.subtitle: How keeping things open helps you make better decisions

sections.text: When you buy a larger hard drive, you don’t become more organized; you just stop deleting what is useless. Available space often dictates how much mental and physical clutter we are willing to tolerate.

Abundance makes us lazy. When space is plentiful, we defer difficult choices because there is no immediate cost to keeping everything. Eventually, the volume of options paralyzes our ability to act and think decisively.

This applies to your digital environment, too. A cluttered screen forces your brain to process noise before it can process meaning. Mental space is the primary prerequisite for high-speed, high-quality thinking.
Try this today: When you look at your computer screen today, close every window you aren't currently using.
Clarity is the byproduct of what you choose to leave out.

news.title: Trump energy secretary says gas prices might not drop back under $3 a gallon until 2027
news.description:
Chris Wright says ‘I don’t know’ when asked about lower cost of gas as average price soars to $4 a gallon in US

Chris Wright, the Trump administration’s energy secretary, acknowledged Sunday that it might not be until 2027 before US gas prices come back under $3 a gallon.

Asked by Jake Tapper, the CNN State of the Union host, when he thought “it’s realistic for Americans to expect the gas will go back to under $3 a gallon”, Wright replied: “I don’t know. That could happen later this year. That might not happen until next year.”

news.title: DR Congo, AFC/M23 group agree to facilitate aid, release prisoners within 10 days
news.description: The DR Congo government and the AFC/M23 group announced Sunday they had reached an agreement to facilitate humanitarian aid deliveries and release prisoners within 10 days. The Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 group has seized large swaths of territory in the eastern part of DR Congo since 2021.

news.title: Apple’s major MacBook Pro overhaul is reportedly ‘slightly’ delayed due to supply chain shortages
news.description:
A lot of us are impatiently awaiting the next-generation of MacBook Pro, which is expected to feature a bevy of updates including a new OLED display with Dynamic Island cutout, a touch screen a la iPad and iPhone, and the more powerful M6 Pro and M6 Max chip.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is today reporting in his newsletter that Apple is facing some production issues due to the industry-wide memory shortages. Supply constraints mean that the MacBook Pro launch is slightly delayed, and possibly won’t arrive until early next year.
